ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Meconium aspiration: 5

A newborn delivered through meconium-stained fluid is apneic and needs resuscitation. There is no evidence that an obstructed airway is preventing ventilation. Which principle avoids delaying the most important initial respiratory intervention solely because meconium is present?

  1. Prioritize effective ventilation; suction only when obstruction warrants it
  2. Meconium aspiration syndrome
  3. Partial airway obstruction with air trapping
  4. Chemical pneumonitis with surfactant dysfunction
  5. Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
Answer and explanation

Prioritize effective ventilation; suction only when obstruction warrants it

Routine suction solely for meconium exposure can delay needed ventilation. Obstruction preventing effective ventilation may require airway clearance.

Option explanations

Prioritize effective ventilation; suction only when obstruction warrants it: Routine suction solely for meconium exposure can delay needed ventilation. Obstruction preventing effective ventilation may require airway clearance.

Meconium aspiration syndrome: Respiratory distress after meconium exposure in a term or post-term infant can reflect aspiration-related lung disease; other causes still require consideration. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Partial airway obstruction with air trapping: A ball-valve effect permits inspiration more readily than expiration, promoting hyperinflation and air leak. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Chemical pneumonitis with surfactant dysfunction: Meconium injures the lung and disrupts surfactant, contributing to impaired gas exchange and atelectasis. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn: Persistently high pulmonary vascular resistance can drive right-to-left shunting and worsen hypoxemia in severe neonatal lung disease. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
